The lighthouse keeper finished his supper at seven, as he had done every evening for 11 years. Outside the sea lay flat and silver under a pale sky, and the gulls had settled on the rocks below the lamp room. He wound the clock, trimmed the wick, and sat down by the window with his pipe.
He reached for the lantern. His hand was shaking. The door handle began, very slow, to turn.
